title: The barrage at El Alamein
body:
At 9:40 p.m. the desert lit up like day.

23 October 1942. Nearly 900 British and Commonwealth guns opened fire at once along the line at El Alamein in Egypt. It was the start of Operation Lightfoot, and the noise rolled across the sand for miles.

Behind the barrage, Montgomery's Eighth Army began clearing paths through the minefields the Germans called the Devil's Gardens.

The timing was cruel for the other side. Rommel was in Germany on sick leave. His stand in, General Georg Stumme, died of a heart attack the next day while driving to the front. Rommel flew back to a battle already underway.

Twelve days later, on 4 November, he ordered the retreat. Back in London, Churchill told the country it was perhaps "the end of the beginning."
